newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Titan starts work on petrochem phase II.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Titan starts work on petrochem phase II.

text.p: Titan Petrochemical (M) Sdn Bhd, a unit of Taiwan's Titan group, said on Wednesday it has started work on the three billion ringgit, second phase of its petrochemical complex.
It said an agreement had been signed with Japan's JGC Corporation and JGC's Malaysian unit for the construction of a second flexible naphtha/LPG cracker.
Phase one was completed in 1994 at a cost of two billion ringgit.
A statement from Titan said the company was also looking to expand in the aromatics business and set up a co-generation power plant to utilise fuel gas from the two crackers.
It said it wanted to set up a polypropylene plant of 170,000 tonnes a year, a 200,000 tonnes capacity low-density polyethylene (LDPE) unit and 100,000 tonnes line of polyethylene.

Also included in the expansion plan announced in August are a 200,000 tonne vinyl chloride monomer (VCM) plant, a 200,000 tonne polyvinyl chloride (PVC) unit and a 300,000 tonne ethylene oxide/ethylene glycol plant.
At present, the petrochemical complex consists of a cracker, a polyethylene plant and a polypropylene unit.
